text: The doctor was good and the staff were helpful, but the queue management was poor. I had an appointment at 1 PM but didn't get to see the patient until 3:30 PM. I'm not sure why we even bothered putting people on the waiting list if we weren't going to follow the queue.

This orthodontic treatment has come a really long way! I'm using the Alexander technique, which is quite detailed and meticulous. I've received many compliments from friends, family, and hotel guests. If I had followed my appointments regularly, my teeth would probably be perfectly aligned and finished much sooner!😅 Even though I haven't been to the dentist often, my teeth are still beautifully aligned. The technique and tooth extraction are also different from other places. From what I've gathered from my friends, my costs are higher than theirs if calculated as a lump sum, but I didn't have as many additional hidden costs as they did. Everything went exactly as we discussed with the dentist. My friend has already had her braces removed, and her teeth are quite spaced apart. She had 4+4 teeth extracted upper and lower, while I had 5+5 extracted upper and lower (the dentist recommended extracting only 5 teeth for a better and more aesthetically pleasing result). The dentist here is very attentive to detail and spends a considerable amount of time with us. We were able to communicate and come to an agreement with the dentist; he's easy to talk to and kind, and the nurses are lovely too.☺️🥰

(Original review) My first visit to get composite resin veneers on my front teeth.
The first time, I had problems with food getting stuck in the brackets and the gap between the fillings was not aesthetically pleasing. The clinic scheduled another appointment for a dental correction. The same dentist meticulously corrected my front teeth, and the results were excellent and beautiful. I was very satisfied.

So, I decided to choose another dental clinic to support this clinic.

While taking the impressions, the technician at this clinic was a woman with a pale complexion wearing a headscarf, probably not yet middle-aged, who instructed me to bite on a mold made of something like wax. When I bit into it, it hurt in my mouth. It might have been due to the soreness from two previous dental procedures, which we don't know. Before the impressions were made, we informed the female dentist who examined us that we had just had dental impressions made by a male dentist. He had advised us not to bite anything at all, as our original tissue had already thinned considerably. However, the technique still advised us to bite hard, stating that it might hurt the bone. At that time, the pain spread throughout my gums and mouth.

Finally, something occurred that I suspected: after I went home and brushed my teeth, I felt that the corrected tooth was protruding further than it should have been.

The clinic called me in for a correction, but upon entering the examination room, we encountered the technician who was having issues. There was no other doctor in the room, only Dear and the technician.

The technician became irritated and displeased, as we suspected it might have been caused by the impressions. He spoke very rudely to us, even telling us to go somewhere else to have our treatment done. He spoke in a very rude manner several times, even demanding a refund and the removal of the dental equipment. His behavior was unacceptable. This led us to respond with words of caution, explaining that we were customers and had paid every baht. We had no intention of demanding a refund. We were simply curious and wanted the doctor to examine us and listen to our reasons to resolve our concerns. This led to Dear's intervention and the situation calming down. Dear informed us that she would report the incident to management and impose disciplinary action on the technician. We insisted on having her personally call and apologize. Ultimately, the clinic, through Dear, personally called to apologize on behalf of the technician, stating that management had decided to suspend the technician and refund the full amount of the denture appointment. The clinic reasoned that there was currently no technician to oversee the procedure. We believed this and did not pursue any legal action, considering it a merit-making gesture and not wanting to harm the organization because of one person.

However, I want everyone reading this to take this as a cautionary tale about encountering the technician in question: This person is unsuitable for this profession. This person, who has been in the news, is considered highly emotionally dangerous.

If you encounter a casual customer and encounter such an ill-mannered individual, I don't know how much other customers at the clinic will spread the word or what criticisms they might receive.

But we commend the management for resolving the issue and hope our case serves as an example to prevent similar problems in the future. "One bad fish kills the entire pond," says a Thai proverb that applies to all eras. A reputation isn't easily built, but it can be destroyed just as easily by one person. This is especially true in service industries, which rely on customers willing to pay for quality treatment.
